observations:
Torah #20 yields 7 packages from 22 bechina edges and 35 nodes. No independent bechina cluster outside these 7 packages exists in the current dataset.

The teaching's structure (eitza chain between packages):
  [Pkg 7: משה/דעת/פגם] → eitza → [Pkg 1: חטם/יראה/תפלה] → eitza → [Pkg 2: לב העליון/סלע] → eitza → [Pkg 5: באורי התורה] → eitza → [Pkg 4: מטה/שערי ציון] → eitza → [Eretz Yisrael]

The good/evil mirror structure:
  Package 2 (לב העליון — holy heart) ←mirrors→ Package 3 (קלפות סביב הלב — the evil besieging forces)
  Package 5 (באורי התורה — Torah interpretation, the well) ←mirrors→ Package 6 (דבור מצנן — cold/frozen speech)
  Package 7's evil pole (פגם הברית/פגם הדעת) mirrors Package 7's good pole (משה/דעת) — internally mirrored within Package 7 itself

CONSIDERATION: The angels/spiritual-forces domain (מלאכים, כוחות רוחניות, אמרות טהורות/יתן אמר המבשרות) could form a new package if bechina edges were added to the dataset. The text in sections ז-ח uses bechina language to equate: (a) כוחות רוחניות הנבראים מחידושי תורה = מלאכים ממש, (b) מלאכים = 'יתן אמר המבשרות צבא רב', (c) מלאכים משרתים = 'אש לוהט' (Psalms 104). Three concepts with explicit bechina language, forming a distinct domain: the creative spiritual forces born from Torah innovation. These currently have no bechina edges in the dataset for reference=20 — they appear only in eitza edges (Torah → creates angels → punish wicked). RECOMMENDATION: If the bechina edges מלאכים↔כוחות רוחניות and מלאכים↔'יתן אמר המבשרות' are added to the dataset for ref=20, a new Package 8 (מַלְאָכִים וְכוֹחוֹת רוּחָנִיּוֹת — Angels and Spiritual Forces, polarity: good) would emerge with 3+ nodes.

A NOTE ON TIKUN STRUCTURE: Torah #20's second half (sections ו-ט and the Pirkei d'Tzniuta commentary) uses the nine tikunei dikna as nine bechina-rich images. The dataset has captured some of these (particularly tikunim 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 partially) but many bechina equations in the tikun commentaries lack corresponding dataset edges. The gap analysis (torah_20_additions.json) documents the priority additions.
